title: Efficient Reasoning Models: A Survey
actual_read_scope: arXiv HTML v2 abstract, introduction, taxonomy/contents, Sections 2-5 (especially 3.1-3.3, 4.1, 5), Appendix A.2-A.4, and the complete reference list; no cited paper was read beyond the survey.

routes.problem: Long or overthinking CoTs waste generated tokens and can hurt accuracy.
routes.mechanism: Add length/accuracy-aware rewards, budgets, or pairwise preferences in RL; allocate more reasoning to hard inputs.
routes.token_connection: Direct: optimizes output-token count or a per-instance budget while preserving answer accuracy.

routes.problem: Fixed long CoT supervision does not teach controllable concise reasoning.
routes.mechanism: Compress or select short correct traces, generate traces at multiple effort levels, and train standard/progressive SFT or DPO.
routes.token_connection: Direct: conditions or trains the model to emit fewer reasoning tokens.

routes.problem: The same inference budget is spent on easy and hard questions.
routes.mechanism: Concise instructions, token-budget estimation, shorthand/symbolic sketches, and classifier/uncertainty routing select shorter paths or smaller models.
routes.token_connection: Direct for output shortening; routing also reduces model-side compute and may change the token target.

routes.problem: Explicit intermediate language tokens are a verbose interface for internal computation.
routes.mechanism: Distill hidden states, recycle continuous hidden states, use auxiliary latent-token modules, looped transformers, or mix text and VQ-VAE tokens; compress KV-visible steps.
routes.token_connection: Direct when latent steps replace explicit CoT tokens; latency gains can instead reflect architecture/KV changes and are not automatically equivalent to fewer compute steps.

routes.problem: Large reasoning models impose parameter, memory, and per-token compute costs.
routes.mechanism: Transfer CoT/PoT, long/short, counterfactual, feedback-refined, or simplified reasoning data to a small student.
routes.token_connection: Indirect for token-count objective; direct for model-size and per-token compute. Student may still produce long CoTs.

routes.problem: Parameter representation and redundant weights increase deployment cost.
routes.mechanism: PTQ/QAT, structured/unstructured/semi-structured pruning, and importance-based compression.
routes.token_connection: Compute/memory only in this survey; no claim that generated reasoning-token count falls. Hardware support determines actual latency.

routes.problem: Small models lack reasoning ability even when their inference footprint is low.
routes.mechanism: Use GRPO/RL and curated blended data to improve reasoning in 1.5B-scale models.
routes.token_connection: Indirect: lowers parameter-side cost; token efficiency is not the optimization target unless reward includes length.

routes.problem: Best-of-N/tree/test-time sampling spends work on low-quality branches.
routes.mechanism: Speculative rejection, early consistency/path evaluation, value prediction, foresight trajectories, dynamic tree search, and state merging.
routes.token_connection: Indirect/direct at decoding budget level: reduces redundant sampled tokens or branches, while a single accepted answer may have unchanged length.

routes.problem: Repeated samples and voting create redundant decoding.
routes.mechanism: Confidence/difficulty-aware early stopping, prefix reuse, perplexity pruning, confidence-weighted voting, or distilled calibration.
routes.token_connection: Direct for aggregate sampled-token count; per-sample CoT length need not change.

routes.problem: Autoregressive serial decoding and repeated subproblem work create latency overhead.
routes.mechanism: Decompose into atoms/DAGs, skeleton-then-fill, graph decoding, parallel branches, and dynamic early stopping.
routes.token_connection: Primarily latency/parallelism; total generated tokens may stay constant or increase, so classify as compute/decoding efficiency unless token accounting is shown.

routes.problem: Accuracy and efficiency are often reported separately, obscuring the Pareto curve.
routes.mechanism: Token count, latency, model size, ACU, optimal token budget, outcome/process efficiency, overthinking, reasoning boundary, underthinking, and AES.
routes.token_connection: Defines the measurement contract for performance versus generated tokens; survey warns token count is not always deployment latency.

candidates.title: L1: Controlling how long a reasoning model thinks with reinforcement learning
candidates.reason: Introduces length-constraint instructions in training data and RL control of reasoning duration; a clean direct precedent for a token-budget objective.

candidates.title: O1-Pruner: Length-harmonizing fine-tuning for o1-like reasoning pruning
candidates.reason: Uses length and accuracy baselines in reward and proposes AES; survey table reports GSM8K 96.50%/543 tokens and 1.5–2.0x latency speedup.

candidates.title: DAST: Difficulty-adaptive slow-thinking for large reasoning models
candidates.reason: Token Length Budget penalizes verbose easy answers while preserving budget for hard ones; exemplifies per-instance performance–token allocation.

candidates.title: TokenSkip: Controllable chain-of-thought compression in LLMs
candidates.reason: Selects/skips low-semantic-contribution tokens and trains controllable short CoT; survey reports 78.20% GSM8K and 1.7–1.8x latency speedup.

candidates.title: CoT-Valve: Length-compressible chain-of-thought tuning
candidates.reason: Uses parameter-space direction/model merging and progressive SFT for length control; introduces ACU combining accuracy, parameters, and token count.

candidates.title: Chain of Draft: Thinking faster by writing less
candidates.reason: Few-shot prompt asks for at most five words per thought step; survey records strong token reduction but explicitly notes degradation in zero-shot and small-model settings.

candidates.title: Sketch-of-Thought: Efficient LLM reasoning with adaptive cognitive-inspired sketching
candidates.reason: Routes inputs to compact conceptual, symbolic, or expert-lexicon sketches; survey reports 3.6x token speedup but no accuracy in Table 2.

candidates.title: Implicit chain of thought reasoning via knowledge distillation
candidates.reason: Seminal latent route: student mimics hidden states of explicit-CoT teacher and later removes teacher at inference; direct replacement of explicit reasoning tokens, though reported GSM8K accuracy is only 20% in the survey table.

candidates.title: Coconut: Chain of continuous thought
candidates.reason: Feeds final-layer hidden states back without decoding text, enabling continuous reasoning, backtracking, and parallel decoding; survey reports GSM8K 34.10% with 8 tokens and 3x token speedup.

candidates.title: CODI: Compressing chain-of-thought into continuous space via self-distillation
candidates.reason: Self-distills explicit LM CoT and implicit hidden activation immediately before the answer; direct continuous compression, with low GPT-2-small GSM8K accuracy (43.70%) in the survey table.

candidates.title: SoftCoT: Soft chain-of-thought for efficient reasoning with LLMs
candidates.reason: A lightweight assistant generates implicit representations conditioned on input; survey reports 85.81% GSM8K and 4–5x latency speedup, making it a key latent performance–latency candidate.

candidates.title: LightThinker: Thinking step-by-step compression
candidates.reason: Segments CoT and compresses each step into special tokens with attention masks and KV-cache focus; survey reports 90.14% GSM8K and up to 1.4x latency speedup.

candidates.title: Deepscaler: Surpassing o1-preview with a 1.5B model by scaling RL
candidates.reason: Shows small-model reasoning can improve through RL, but the survey gives no token count and cites a Notion blog rather than an arXiv paper; model-size gain must not be treated as token compression.

candidates.title: φ-decoding: Adaptive foresight sampling for balanced inference-time exploration and exploitation
candidates.reason: Simulates future paths and clusters their distributions to choose each next step; survey reports 2.8x inference speedup and +6.14% accuracy, but this is decoding compute/latency rather than necessarily fewer final answer tokens.

candidates.title: Path-consistency: Prefix enhancement for efficient inference in LLM
candidates.reason: Reuses high-confidence prefixes across samples to accelerate self-consistency; survey reports +3.80% GSM8K and 1.2x latency speedup, with aggregate-sampling savings rather than a shorter CoT target.

candidates.title: When more is less: Understanding chain-of-thought length in LLMs
candidates.reason: Survey cites it as evidence that longer CoT can yield negative returns and accumulated errors; it is a necessary counterexample against equating more tokens with better reasoning.

gaps/conflicts: The taxonomy cleanly separates shorter, smaller, and faster, but latent reasoning, KV/context compression, architecture changes, routing, and parallel decoding cross boundaries; assign the primary route by the measured resource and retain secondary links.

The survey often reports token count, latency, model size, or sampling count separately; a lower token count is not automatically lower end-to-end latency, and fewer sampled paths is not necessarily a shorter accepted CoT.

Latent methods claim explicit-token compression, yet early entries have weak GSM8K accuracy (Implicit-KD 20%, SI 30%, CCoT 17.90%, CODI 43.70%, Coconut 34.10% in Table 2). These are evidence-boundary/counterexample signals, not validated superiority.

Smaller-model RL/KD and quantization/pruning are mainly parameter, memory, or per-token-compute improvements. The survey explicitly says LoRA savings apply to training and do not reduce inference memory; quantization/pruning do not imply fewer reasoning tokens.

The survey's reported token–latency correlation (Pearson 0.9998 on Qwen2.5-7B/MAHT-500) is one model/dataset result; it does not replace deployment measurements across hardware, batching, parallelism, or KV-cache policy.
Reported benchmark rows mix base models, datasets, decoding protocols, and accuracy scales; they are candidate evidence for a performance–token curve, not a fair cross-paper ranking.

Version coverage is fixed at v2, last revised 2025-09-29 (TMLR 2025). No later revision was visible on the arXiv record as of 2026-09-09; the survey cannot cover post-v2 work, including later latent/architecture/decoding papers.

Training-efficiency items in §5 (Light-R1, FASTCURL, DAPO, LIMO, s1) were excluded from candidates unless they directly affect inference-time token/size/decoding behavior; they are background only for this map.
